svg.title: 1. The four DR strategies side by side
svg.text: Four AWS disaster recovery strategies: what runs in the recovery Region, and what it buys you
more running in the recovery Region = lower RTO and RPO, higher cost and complexity
Running DR cost: about 5% of prod
RPO seconds to minutes · RTO tens of minutes
RTO = scale out + promote (20 to 60 min)
Running DR cost: about 10 to 20% of prod
RTO = scale up + switch (5 to 20 min)
Running DR cost: about 30 to 50% of prod
RPO near zero · RTO near zero
RPO = zero to seconds (by data store)
RTO = stop routing to one Region
All four keep data outside the primary Region. What changes is how much of the application is already running when disaster is declared.
Backup and restore rebuilds everything from code and recovery points. Pilot light keeps the data live and the compute switched off.
Warm standby runs a smaller, working copy of the whole stack. Active/active runs the full stack in both Regions and serves users from both.
Cost bars are the running cost of the recovery Region for the example workload in this article, as a share of the primary Region.
